## 1. The question, frozen

The paper answers several questions. The one its opening makes central: *describe the diagnostic and therapeutic trajectories of three patients with SSc-ILD who developed lung cancer, and draw out real-world considerations.* That is mainly the backward kind — "what can we tell from what we see" — though the Key Messages and Discussion bolt forward claims ("what produces it") onto it. I hold the descriptive question still and test the causal add-ons as parts of it. Range: three patients, one academic safety-net centre, 2019–2023.

## 2. The jobs and the parts

**Jobs:** (J1) why these patients got cancer, as a contrast with who doesn't; (J2) why the cancer was hard to find; (J3) whether immunosuppression should be held or continued. All three are the owner's own (given), not added.

**Parts:** P1 SSc-ILD raises lung-cancer risk four-fold, and ILD raises it further. P2 chronic inflammation, fibrosis and immune dysregulation drive it. P3 scarred parenchyma hides nodules. P4 PET/CT plus a lower biopsy threshold finds them. P5 holding immunosuppression during cancer treatment worsens ILD. P6 mycophenolate and chemotherapy overlap, so restarting is risky. P7 multidisciplinary co-management is essential. P8 the safety-net setting adds follow-up obstacles.

## 3. Part by part

| Part | Mark | Why |
|---|---|---|
| P1 risk | **Borrowed** | Rests on the cited epidemiology, not on three cases. The paper says so. |
| P2 mechanism | **Borrowed**, partly a label | "Pro-oncogenic microenvironment" names the thing to be explained. "May promote" is an assertion; held by translational studies not tested here. |
| P3 hard to find | **Held** | The cases supply the contrast: case 1's biopsy was non-diagnostic; every diagnosis needed extra steps. |
| P4 PET/CT, low threshold | **Held if** | Held by the route to diagnosis, but undercut by the paper's own admission that ILD inflammation gives FDG avidity — so "intense avidity" can't be read straight off as cancer. |
| P5 pausing worsens ILD | **Held if** | All three paused and all three progressed — consistent, but no case is reported that paused and stayed well, and two setbacks are "attributed to" a cause. That word is doing causal work. The pull it names is real; three cases alone don't hold it. |
| P6 drug overlap | **Borrowed** | Two drugs hitting dividing cells is a genuine mechanism, and cited — not tested here. |
| P7 MDT | **Held if / loose** | No case where co-management was absent and care went worse. |
| P8 safety-net | **Idle** | One sentence, one citation, no case detail; removing it loses nothing. |

## 4. Whole-explanation checks

**Flip.** Take P5. Suppose a patient had held mycophenolate and stayed well. Would we read that here? The three were selected *because* they were co-managed and ill, so the opposite outcome is off the change list. Same for P3: patients whose nodules were never caught never appear.

**Reverse.** P5 is stated as production (pausing causes worsening) but read off outcomes. Poke the cause and the effect moves; the paper never shows the other direction.

**Answer hidden in the start.** P2 puts the conclusion inside the starting point: "inflammation and immune dysregulation" is what we would say even with no idea how the cancer arose.

**Pairs that pull.** The named tension — immunosuppression protects lungs, hold it and the tumour may grow — is the best-held piece here. One pair, clearly drawn.

**Catch-all.** "Management is often individualized through multidisciplinary discussion" absorbs any decision, with no gauge. What reading would show the MDT changed an outcome?

**Change list.** The comparisons the paper needs — SSc-ILD patients without cancer, other centres, other intervals — aren't there. It says this plainly ("precludes inference regarding risk, causality, mechanisms"). A stated limit is the honest version, not a fault.

**Rivals.** P2's rival (smoking alone) is met by case 1, a never-smoker — though two of three were ex-smokers, so the smoking-independent claim rests on one case. P5's rival (the cancer, not the pause, drove the decline) is not ruled out.

**Where the parts came from.** P1, P2, P6 are borrowed. P3 and P4 are fitted to the three cases. Nothing is built against changes not yet met.

## 5. What would make it harder to vary

Two moves. (a) Report the missing flips: SSc-ILD patients paused and stable, and nodules that proved benign. Those contrasts could kill P5 and P4 and don't exist here. (b) Give P7 a gauge — name one decision the MDT actually changed.

## 6. What this does not show

Passing is not truth. P1 and P2 may well be right; this paper doesn't hold them. The descriptive job — the trajectories — is done, and the limits are stated.

## 7. One next step

For P5, write down for one patient the change that would have counted against it (a paused interval with stable ILD), then count how many such intervals the record contains.
